## Historical audit — S0313

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v3/results/H02/selection/bw_0017/1/trajectory.jsonl`. Only chunk 1 of 2 is visible; citations below refer to its JSONL lines. No images were independently inspected in this audit.

| Evidence | Observation and limits |
|---|---|
| Goal — H `model_request`, line 1 | Reconstruct a 512 × 267 indoor photograph as separate SceneAct/Blender meshes, matching camera, framing, materials and occlusion. The inferred semantic goal is a visually faithful industrial-hall scene; the image itself is not available here for independent confirmation. |
| Initial build — H `model_response` line 3; `execute` line 4 | The program describes and constructs multiple assets: hall, raised platform, three machines and stairs, ducts, tank, and conveyors. It emits named parts including supports, railings, treads, pipe segments and tank legs. These are authored relationships, not proof of correct physical connections or reference coverage. Colored materials, metallic/roughness settings, camera pose and area lights are coded; no external texture is used. |
| First validation — `build_completed` line 6, `render_completed` line 8, `execution_result` line 9, `select` line 10 | Build and render returned zero; `ok: true`, a PNG path and step-1 selection are recorded. This establishes execution success, not image similarity. |
| Revision — H request line 11; response line 13; `execute` line 14 | The student received the reference and first render in a comparison request. Its own diagnosis was exterior roof/blank background, undersized foreground, sloping rails and sparse detail. It moved the camera inside and closer, extended the hall, changed machine fronts and added a fourth conveyor and open frames. It said it would increase lens, but the code changes 34 to 32. These visual diagnoses are student claims, not independently verified findings. |
| Second validation and revision — `execution_result` line 19; `select` line 20; H request line 21; response line 23; `execute` line 24 | Step 2 reports success and is selected. After being supplied its render, H claimed stairs were too vertical, ceiling coverage too small, foreground too thin and machines too bright. It shifted camera x from 2 to −5, aimed higher, extended the hall, repositioned conveyors, darkened materials and adjusted lights. Whether these changes improved pose, framing, connections or appearance is unverified. |
| Third execution — `build_completed` line 26; `render_completed` line 28 | Both stages report completion and zero return code. No subsequent execution result, selection, final review or final submission is visible in this chunk. |

**Input and exploration.** No distinct teacher intervention, teacher diagnosis or teacher-proposed update is visible. The comparison instructions and rendered images in H requests are actual runner/user feedback, not evidence of a separate teacher. H independently produced two diagnosed revisions after that feedback; its sessions report no tool calls (lines 2, 12, 22). This does not establish unseen exploration or teacher receipt.

**Outcome and uncertainty.** Three builds and renders completed technically; the overall reconstruction outcome is **unknown**, not a verified formal success, algorithm failure, empty patch or interruption. Neither the final image nor chunk 2 is visible. Thus actual object completeness, texture fidelity, part contact, pose, lighting and camera accuracy remain unresolved. A transferable observation is that executable renders permit iterative, anchor-based diagnosis, but successful execution does not validate visual fidelity. The particular roof crop, conveyor placement and camera-direction diagnoses are task-specific hypotheses until independently compared with the images.
